lifecycle_gaps_retained: Whether the 'sexual orientation, gender identity' wording inserted into EO 11478 section 1 survives in the printed text of EO 11478 after 14173 revoked 13672 (current text of EO 11478 as of 2026-10-14 not held); the U.S. Code note that still prints 13672 section 1 is editorial and not a current predicate.
notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held text of EO 13672, its single API observation (a 2026-10-15 Federal Register disposition note naming a revocation by EO 14173), the acting text of EO 14173, and the U.S. Code current-law lead. The API note and the U.S. Code note are leads only; the basis is the held text of EO 14173. EO 13672 (signed 2014-07-21, 79 FR 42971) section 1 amends section 1 of EO 11478 and section 2 amends EO 11246, section 3 directs the Secretary of Labor to prepare regulations, section 4 is general provisions and section 5 sets the effective date. Executive Order 14173 (signed 2025-01-21, 90 FR 8633) section 3(a)(iii) says that Executive Order 13672 of July 21, 2014 is among the executive actions hereby revoked, with no delayed effective date for subsection (a) in the held text. The 90-day contractor transition in section 3(b)(i) concerns the revocation of EO 11246, not 13672. So every clause of 13672 was revoked by name on 2025-01-21. Partial scope: section 2 also fell with its parent EO 11246 (revoked by 14173 section 3(b)(i)). Section 1 amended EO 11478, which 14173 does not revoke; the revocation of the amending order by name is the reason I treat section 1 as ended, but whether the substituted wording in EO 11478 survives as text is a separate lifecycle question left to the clause review.
